purpose: Rules for running Python scripts and managing dependencies with uv, so that uv selects and records version numbers and people and AI never write them by hand.
summary: Applicability: applies when project instructions mandate uv; adoption for distributed scripts is a user-environment decision
Where to declare dependencies: PEP 723 inline metadata for standalone or distributed scripts, pyproject.toml for script groups with shared modules and tests
Execution: run Python scripts with uv run, declare Python and dependencies in PEP 723 metadata, keep tool.uv settings in the metadata
Adding and removing dependencies: get user permission, use uv add --script with --bounds lower and uv remove --script, never hand-write versions
Locking: uv lock --script, commit the lock file with the script, use uv run --locked to detect mismatches
Updating: check with uv tree --outdated, upgrade with uv lock --upgrade or --upgrade-package, review the lock diff before commit
Excluding freshly published versions: exclude-newer = "3 days" to mitigate supply-chain attacks, with a per-package exception for urgent security fixes
Python version: requires-python lower bound follows the latest stable release, excluding alpha, beta and rc, checked via uv python list
tasks: Writing or running a Python script in a plugin
Adding or removing a script dependency
Setting up pyproject.toml for a group of scripts and tests
Creating or updating a uv lock file
Running unit tests with uv run --locked
